forecasts.name: Land-Grab Realist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: With prices already at $237 and momentum strong amid Black Sea port attacks, reaching $250 by year-end is probable as importers scramble for prompt feed cargoes.

forecasts.name: Climate Pessimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Severe drought in Southern Europe has starved feed balances. Upward momentum from $237 to $250 by December will be sustained by buyer hoarding.

forecasts.name: BirdLife Europe, EEB, WWF and Greenpeace (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Summer heat anomalies and disrupted Black Sea flows are sustaining feed grain tightness, making a rise above $250 very achievable by December.

forecasts.name: Geopolitics Hawk · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Maize shows strong upward momentum from $213 to $237. Escalating Black Sea risks will spur precautionary procurement by December.

forecasts.name: Macro / Dollar · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Current broad ag strength and fund positioning provide a firm tailwind for maize to test $250 over the coming two months.

forecasts.name: IMF (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Escalating war risks across Black Sea transit corridors provide immediate upward momentum to European feed import pricing.

forecasts.name: Copa-Cogeca (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Rising feed grain demand and Black Sea shipping disruptions provide strong near-term price support across Southern European import hubs.

forecasts.name: Crowd Follower · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: The crowd sets this at 43%. Maize prices gained strongly in September, warranting a slight follow-through adjustment.

forecasts.name: IFPRI (Joseph Glauber) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Persistent Mediterranean feed deficits and Black Sea logistics friction keep Spanish feed maize prices supported near current levels through December.

forecasts.name: FAO (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Feed grain demand remains steady, but harvest pressure and cheaper alternatives like sorghum cap short-term price spikes before December.

forecasts.name: USDA WASDE (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: With prices at $237/mt, reaching $250/mt by December assumes sudden tightness contrary to ongoing harvest arrivals and balanced feed demand.

forecasts.name: European Commission DG AGRI (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Short-term feed grain supplies remain balanced, making a swift climb past $250/mt before year-end unlikely without severe escalation.

forecasts.name: Scott Irwin (farmdoc) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Markets digest incoming supply quickly. Lingering near production costs usually leads to downside risk rather than a sudden pre-winter jump past $250.

forecasts.name: Adaptation Optimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Strong autumn feed grain availability and easing input costs mitigate near-term upside pressure in European feed markets.

forecasts.name: Efficient-Market Skeptic · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Gaining another $13 in two months after a protracted rise is unlikely. Short-term inertia favors consolidation rather than fresh upward breakouts.

forecasts.name: Agronomist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: December coincides with the peak influx of newly harvested feed maize across Europe. Seasonal harvest arrivals usually depress rather than elevate prices toward $250.
